s1.syndrome_frame: a middle-aged woman with a history of cancer presenting with a new onset of neurological symptoms and a mass lesion in the brain
salient_findings: mass lesion in the right temporal lobe
key_facts: redness and swelling of the right breast
low-echo mass with partially unclear margins in the outer right breast
increased uptake in the right axilla, anterior mediastinum, left pleura, and liver on PET-CT
received trastuzumab plus pertuzumab with docetaxel
developed persistent headache two years after treatment initiation
30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe on CT and MRI

shortlist.label: Brain Metastasis from Breast Cancer
shortlist.why_kept: history of breast cancer and new mass lesion in the brain

shortlist.label: Glioblastoma Multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: new onset of neurological symptoms and mass lesion in the brain

shortlist.label: Leptomeningeal Carcinomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: history of breast cancer and new neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Radiation Necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: history of chemotherapy and radiation treatment for breast cancer

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: new onset of neurological symptoms and mass lesion in the brain

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of stage IV breast cancer with known metastases to multiple sites, and now presents with a mass lesion in the brain, which is a common site for breast cancer metastasis.

rejected.label: Glioblastoma Multiforme
rejected.why: No prior evidence of primary brain tumor and the patient's history of metastatic breast cancer makes this less likely

rejected.label: Leptomeningeal Carcinomatosis
rejected.why: The presentation of a discrete mass lesion rather than diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement suggests a focal process like metastasis

rejected.label: Radiation Necrosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient receiving radiation therapy to the brain, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's history and the presence of a single mass lesion in the context of known metastatic disease makes lymphoma less likely
